step.galaxy: Travel to the galaxy shown in the card.
step.portal: Travel through a portal with these glyphs.
step.take: Go to the coordinates shown in the card and take it.
step.staff: Go to the coordinates shown in the card. With a Scan Harmoniser or a Polyphonic Core in your multitool, scan beside the building until the Synthesis Terminal appears, then assemble a staff there with the head shown in the card.
step.pillarFly: Without loading another save, fly to the planet shown in the card and take the tool from any sentinel pillar there; one stands at the coordinates shown in the card.
step.pillarHere: Without loading another save, take the tool from any sentinel pillar on this planet; one stands at the coordinates shown in the card.
step.shopFly: Without loading another save, fly to the planet shown in the card, go to the coordinates shown there, and buy the tool from the weapon cabinet in the shop.
step.shopHere: Without loading another save, go to the coordinates shown in the card and buy the tool from the weapon cabinet in the shop.
step.monolithFly: Without loading another save, fly to the planet shown in the card, go to the coordinates shown there, and take the tool from the monolith.
step.monolithHere: Without loading another save, go to the coordinates shown in the card and take the tool from the monolith.
step.stationHere: Without loading another save, fly to the system's space station and buy the tool from the weapon cabinet.
step.leaveMessage: Build a Communications Station here to leave a mark for other travellers.
step.find: This creature lives {habitat} and is active {time}. Go and look for it.
step.saveLoad: Save the game here and load that save.

archive.homeTitle: How to get the best item in No Man's Sky
archive.homeLead: Pick up a <tools>multitool</tools> with four adjacent supercharged slots, claim a <ships>crashed ship</ships>, or adopt a <creatures>creature</creatures>, each with the portal glyphs and coordinates to get there. The <guides>guides</guides> say where each kind of item comes from, from the galaxy down to the planet, and <lucky>How lucky am I?</lucky> scores one you found yourself. The <capital>capital freighters</capital> page shows every capital freighter shape, the <interceptor>Sentinel Interceptors</interceptor> page shows every Interceptor the game can build, and <about>how it works</about> tells why only a few systems make the list.

kindLead.tool: Every multitool here has its four supercharged slots side by side at class S, staffs among them, and many lie below S: the slots stay when you pay for the upgrade, and <upgrade>how to upgrade a multitool</upgrade> says what else changes. Where <classes>class S multitools</classes> come from, and which <staffs>staff head</staffs> to fit, are in the guides.
kindLead.ship: Every crashed ship here has four supercharged slots side by side, whatever its class. <classes>Ship classes</classes> says which wreck is class S, and <upgrade>how to upgrade a ship</upgrade> what an upgrade gives. Interceptors are among them, and the <finder>Sentinel Interceptors</finder> page shows every form they take.
kindLead.creature: Every creature here can be adopted, whatever its grades. How rare an all-S creature is, and where to look for one, is under <grades>creature grades</grades>.
kindLead.planet: Each planet here belongs to a listed star system. Which <types>type of planet</types> holds the most spots, and where to find <dissonance>dissonance</dissonance>, are in the guides.
kindLead.system: Each star system here holds the planets of the listed finds. What a <systems>star system</systems> holds, and which <economy>economy</economy> pays best, are in the guides.
kindLead.galaxy: What the type of a galaxy changes, and which one to search, is under <galaxies>galaxies</galaxies>.

luck.head: Head
luck.headHelp: Every head rolls alike, so it does not change the score
luck.required: Enter the number from the game
luck.tooManySlots: Class {klass} holds at most {count} supercharged slots.
luck.fewerSlots: Class holds {count}. Fewer are fine: a supercharged slot can lie in a slot that is still closed, where you cannot see it. Slots then stay out of the score.
luck.readingMisfit: {name} does not fit this type and class.
luck.readingBetter: {name}: better than {share}% of the same type and class.
luck.foundUpgradedStaff: This is an upgraded staff. Every staff upgraded to this class holds these same numbers, so there is no luck in them.
luck.foundUpgraded: This damage cannot come with the class, so this tool was upgraded, not found at it.
luck.slotsBelowS: Below class S it holds fewer than four supercharged slots, so slots stay out of the score.
luck.slotsMarkAll: Mark all four supercharged slots to count them.
luck.slotsSquare: The four slots form a square, the rarest figure.
luck.slotsScattered: The four slots are not adjacent, like most.
luck.noStats: A {type} of class {klass} has no base stats, so there are no numbers to enter.
luck.noFinds: No {type} is found at class {klass}, so there is nothing to compare these numbers with, and they stay out of the score.
